rows.measured: VERDICT - THE 6d EXPONENT IS A CONFINEMENT LAW AND THE MECHANISM IS COLLECTIVE RETURN FLOW, NOT PER-PARTICLE WALL DRAG. (1) Wide single-particle reference: u_t(12d) = 0.4034 +- 0.0064, within 0.7 percent of the 6d u_t = 0.4061 (inside 1 sigma; endpoint drift +2.6e-3 inside the 5e-3 steadiness gate) - an isolated particle at this Re is NOT measurably wall-retarded even in the 6d column, so per-particle wall friction cannot carry the 6d hindrance. (2) The same clouds that settled hindered in the 6d column settle ENHANCED in the 12d column: U/u_t(12d) = 1.046/1.051/1.057 at N=40 (seed span 0.005 in U) and 1.145/1.102/1.162 at N=120 (span 0.024) - enhancement GROWING with N, the opposite sign of hindrance. (3) Two-rung slope in RZ form with cloud-envelope phi (bounding-box: phi_env 0.043 at N=40, 0.071 at N=120): n = -2.63 - negative, i.e. the RZ functional form does not describe a finite cloud in a wide vessel at all. The finite-cloud hypothesis (n stays ~4.5) is REFUTED decisively; the wall hypothesis wins, but as a sign change rather than a drift toward Rowe. MECHANISM: in the 6d column the cloud fills the cross-section and continuity forces the displaced-fluid return flow back through and past the cloud (strong hindrance, n=4.57); in the 12d column the return flow spreads over 4x the area and the cloud's collective downdraft dominates (swarm/blob enhancement). CONSEQUENCE FOR USE: n=4.57 is valid for vessel-filling confined suspensions (cloud/column cross-section ratio ~1) and must NOT be applied as an unbounded hindrance law; Rowe/RZ 2.7-3.0 applies to vessel-filling homogeneous suspensions; finite clouds in wide vessels are a third regime (enhanced settling) in which the EL closure should rely on local-phi hindrance plus the resolved collective flow the EL solver already computes. CAVEAT: phi_env is a bounding-box estimate (mild underestimate of local concentration); area-based numbers reproducible via tools/d32_ladder_analysis.py --ut 0.4034 --area 144.0
